author: /root/runtime_review
kind: production-reference Windows alias correction and negative-stage qualification

sourceCorrection.problem: A bounded snapshot canonical filename was compared directly to the declared config spelling before that declaration was independently canonicalized. Ordinary Windows alias spellings can identify the same file yet fail this mixed-form comparison before native observation.
sourceCorrection.replacement: Compare the complete bounded config identity to the independently canonicalized manager config identity, including filename, device, inode, link count, size, modification time and change time.
sourceCorrection.scope: Only lib/dev-runtime-reference.mjs and test/dev-runtime-reference.test.mjs changed by this correction.

regression.canonicalAliasFixture: Controlled filesystem alias backed by real Windows file/handle identities; explicitly not native 8.3 allocation qualification.
regression.oldGuardContradiction: The case asserts different declared/canonical spelling after case/dot normalization, equal actual snapshot identities/bytes, and a successful full reference inspection. The old mixed-spelling guard rejects this exact condition.
negativeStageAssertions: Wrong-account case passes a matched baseline then measures wrong-profile unverified without production reads.
Config-retarget, control-drift and post-exchange-retarget cases require one attack exchange and mutationApplied true.
Credential cases require a valid baseline, one exchange per fault, and actual DEV plus production credential reads for both equal-digest and plaintext faults.
Topology case passes the original and each restored configuration around three explicit junction/hardlink injections; negative exchange count remains zero.
Privacy case requires successful baseline, actual throwing callback invocation and no invalid-client callback invocation.
